findings.issue: Residual fail-open in the alias merge: a refusal message recorded under one id can be replaced before the link, so the merged record sees no refusal and the build reports completed: true. Each subagent record keeps only its latest error string (classify overwrites r.message on any string, including ''). When the failed state sits under one id and the refusal message under the other, nothing is classified until the linking update. If a later update under the second id carries a plain error or an empty string before that link, merge() finds no refusal message in either record, the result is clean, and readAgy returns the answer (ask-model.mjs:2188 then writes build.completed true). Traced by reading, not run: byConv({status:'ERROR'}), byLog({error:'EPERM …'}), byLog({error:''}) or byLog({error:'command exited 1'}), link(), SUCCESS -> A.failed='ERROR', B.message='' -> [undefined,''].find(...) is undefined -> agyRefusal('ERROR','') is null -> no entry, no exit. The same updates under one id are refused at the second update and a later string cannot clear it, so this breaks A2 ('a later clean/DONE update cannot erase a denial') for the window before the link. Base returned clean for this input too; the branch's merge leaves it open. The new tests only send the clearing updates after the link. Harmed principal: the operator, whose orchestrator receives a native build receipt for a build in which a subagent action was refused.
findings.quote: keep.message = [keep.message, gone.message].find((m) => AGY_DENIALS[agyRefusal('ERROR', m)]) ?? keep.message ?? gone.message;
findings.suggestion: Make a subagent record's refusal message sticky before the merge reads it: in the subagent path, do not let a string that is not a refusal message replace one for which AGY_DENIALS[agyRefusal('ERROR', m)] is set (or keep it in a separate field that merge() consults). Add a fixture: ERROR under conversation_id, EPERM under log_uri, then error '' and a plain error under log_uri, then the link -> exit 4 with one entry. This is the existing pairing rule applied to the pre-link window, not a new refusal kind.
findings.trigger: No observed trigger in normal use (unverified against a live agy stream; no live calls are authorized). It needs agy to (1) split a subagent's failed state and its refusal message across conversation_id and log_uri, the parent gap earlier rated likelihood 2, and additionally (2) send a second error string ('' or a non-permission error) under the message-bearing id before the update that names both ids. Call path: ask-model native agy build -> readAgy -> agyBuildDenials -> merge.
